newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan rebels claim victory at southern garrison.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels claim victory at southern garrison.

text.p: Sudanese rebels fighting towards the major southern town of Juba said on Sunday they had captured an army garrison town on the Juba road.
"Lainya fell to the SPLA yesterday (Saturday) at 1800 hours local time (1600 GMT)," said Samson Kwaje, Nairobi spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army.
He said he received the news from SPLA leader John Garang stationed in Yei, but gave no further details.
Sudanese rebels said on Friday they were advancing towards Lainya after capturing 1,000 government soldiers and a large quantity of weapons when they overran Yei town and Morobo garrison.
Yei, which fell to rebels on Thursday, is the biggest town in Sudan's Western Equatoria region.
In Khartoum, the Sudanese army said on Saturday it had lost contact with its units in Yei but would not say whether the town had fallen.
Lainya, 100 km (63 miles) southwest of Juba, is 60 km (37 miles) northeast of Yei.
The SPLA has been fighting Khartoum since 1983, demanding greater autonomy for the mainly-Christian and animist south of Sudan from the Moslem and Arabised north.
